titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 32/2015 (ޓެރަރިޒަމް މަނާކުރުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ...... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Anti-Terrorism Act (Act No. 32/2015). It adds one new item to the list in Article 4(a) of that Act: damaging a mosque. According to the bill's explanatory note, this places damage to mosques among the acts treated as terrorism. The bill has only two clauses: the amendment itself and a clause saying when it takes effect.
whyItMatters: If passed, damaging a mosque would fall under the Anti-Terrorism Act, so such cases could be handled as terrorism offences rather than under ordinary criminal law.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 adds a new item (8) after item (7) of Article 4(a) of the Anti-Terrorism Act.
The new Article 4(a)(8) reads: damaging a mosque.
Clause 2 says the amendment takes effect on the day it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Anyone who damages a mosque in the Maldives, along with the police, prosecutors and courts who apply the Anti-Terrorism Act.
statedReasons: The note says Article 10 of the Constitution makes Islam the state religion, damage to mosques has become common and keeps happening, and such acts harm the dignity of mosques. It says protecting that dignity is part of respecting Islam, so these acts should be counted as acts of terrorism.
